## My thinking this season

At 1.5 mu, honestly my land is small — it won't feed five people, let alone pay for everything. Two of us work off-farm and that's where the real money comes from. But I've been doing wheat-maize here for 15 years and the land is decent, so I'm not going to farm it carelessly. The grain we keep for the household, and whatever's left we sell locally.

I finished senior high and I've been to a few township training sessions, so I pay attention to fertilizer rates and variety selection. I'm not going to blindly dump urea like my father's generation, but I'm also not going to spend money testing soil every year for 1.5 mu — that makes no sense.

**Winter wheat (Oct → June):** I'll stick with Jimai 22, same as last year. It yielded about 480 kg/mu last season and the quality was good. I'll apply compound fertilizer (15-15-15) as base before planting, around 40 kg/mu, then topdress urea at jointing in March — maybe 15 kg/mu if the crop looks pale, less if it's dark and lodging risk is real. Total N works out to about 13 kg/mu base plus 7 from urea = 20 kg/mu. That matches what I've been doing. Irrigation: once before winter to firm the soil, then jointing and grain-filling if spring is dry. If we get good rain I'll skip one — pumping isn't free.

**Summer maize (June → Sept):** Zhengdan 958 or Denghai 605, whichever the seed shop has fresh. Right after wheat harvest we have maybe 5 days — no time for deep tillage, I'll go straight no-till with a rented planter (one neighbor has one, we share fuel). N rate around 16 kg/mu, split with base at planting and topdress at big-flare stage. Herbicide after planting before emergence — saves a huge amount of weeding labor. Maize here mostly relies on summer rain, I'll only irrigate if July-August turns dry.

Main risk I'm watching: fertilizer prices have been unstable. If urea jumps again I'll pull the topdress rate down by 2-3 kg rather than skipping it.
